newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica financial services seen drawing investment.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica financial services seen drawing investment.

text.p: South Africa's financial services, manufacturing, distribution, communications and transport sectors are the most likely to attract new foreign investment in the next year, according to a survey by a U.S. research group.

The recently completed survey by the Investor Responsibility Research Centre (IRRC) shows that multinational firms doing business in South Africa continue to rate the country better than most other emerging markets.
They rate it better for its infrastructure, legal system and supply of raw materials and praise it for its macroeconomic management, the IRRC said.
But the country's high crime rate and unstable industrial relations were criticised.

"Foreign companies remain extremely critical of South Africa for its high levels of crime and violence, and they believe the country compares poorly with other emerging markets with regard to labour productivity and industrial relations," said Meg Voorhes, director of IRRC's Southern Africa Service.

IRRC said that most foreign firms who said they planned new investments in South Africa within the next year were already investing in the country. "I think we'll see fewer newcomers in the next year," Voorhes said.
About 57 percent of the 356 companies surveyed said they wanted South Africa to lift all foreign exchange controls.
